- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent 10d mean is below 65.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome is <70, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 10d.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% above recent 10d average for next 5d.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast by 3–8% if sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed (0.33–0.67) over last 5d.
